Would be good to know what "the duplicate probe problem" means.  This isn't something I'm familiar with.

Hi Patrick,

We just found the symptom but have not seen the root cause yet. I sent this change first due to the project's tiny schedule and will check the mechanism of EM and FRU devices the reason for this case and will share it with you.
What does the symptom mean?  I don't know what "to avoid the duplicate probe problem" even means.

There are two fan boards connected to the RMC on i2c bus 16/17 with the same FRU information. There are two sources of the fan board with different ADC chips and use the filed Board Custom Data 4 to distinguish.

So we want to use one configuration to cover two fan boards using different buses and the BOARD_INFO_AM4 to distinguish different sources as below format.

```
"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'BOARD_PRODUCT_NAME': 'Ventura FAN Board', 'BUS': 17})",
"AND",
"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'BOARD_INFO_AM4': 'adc-max'})"
```

But we found there will be duplicate probes, below is the portion of the entity manager journal log. The "Ventura Fan Board 0/1" was added two times by each.

```

Mar 19 23:00:14 bmc entity-manager[478]: Inventory Added: BMC Storage Module

```

Then I found the `"BuildDate": "20241216T143500Z"` and `"BuildDate": "20241216T145100Z"` there one is from the EEPROM on bus 16 and another is from bus 17. 

It seems that the EEPROMs on the fan boards are being probed twice.  
I have modified the probe condition to a single line, and it now works fine.  

We have not yet investigated the root cause of this behavior.  
Do you have any insights or comments on this? Is this the expected behavior?
No.  I have not seen this behavior before.  Not sure what would cause it.
Ok, we will investigate this issue and will let you know. Thanks for your review 😊.
